A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ROMBRL research. All 27 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–K, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original policy-evaluation experiments on twelve D4RL MuJoCo tasks and three simulated Tokamak Control tasks, including Tables 1–2 and Appendix K.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, numerical results and training curves, including the Tokamak results in Appendix K.

M1.justification: The constrained maximin objective, Stackelberg updates, Fisher-information approximation, Woodbury computation and gradient masks are unchanged. Appendix J retains the same two algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same twelve MuJoCo task/dataset combinations and three Tokamak tracking tasks for rotation, density and beta_N. Dataset coverage and noisy deployment scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CQL, EDAC, COMBO, RAMBO and MOBILE. Table 2 retains those comparators plus BAMCTS; no comparator is added or removed from either experiment.

E3.justification: Both retain the 5% Gaussian measurement-noise protocol, evaluation over the final 100 policy-learning epochs and the same metrics. Appendix K retains 111305 Tokamak transitions, nine reference shots and identical preprocessing and control settings.

E4.justification: Figure 1's clean-versus-noisy comparison and Section 6's robustness evaluations are unchanged. No ablation, sensitivity study or other supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations across three random seeds and Cohen's d in Tables 1–2. Both omit confidence intervals from the smoothed training curves; run-count and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported table entries and plotted results match. ROMBRL's averages remain 77.7 (0.5) in Table 1 and -47.1 (1.2) in Table 2, with unchanged rankings and findings.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, Theorems 1–4 and mathematical arguments are unchanged. Appendices A–I retain the same proofs, covering-number discussion, approximation-error derivations and complexity analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about robust joint model-policy optimization, Stackelberg learning, theoretical guarantees, computational efficiency and benchmark superiority.

C2.justification: The robustness interpretations and replay-buffer distribution-shift explanation are unchanged. Appendix E still defers neural-network covering bounds to future work, and Appendix H retains the same approximation-error qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendices J–K retain identical implementation and data-processing disclosures, including pseudocode, gradient masks, truncated rollouts and Tokamak state/action construction. No technical or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 51 references are retained, together with the same positioning relative to RAMBO and prior work on robust RL and Stackelberg learning.

P1.justification: v2 adds Le Xu of Tsinghua University to the author list and changes Jiayu Chen's affiliation and email from Carnegie Mellon University to The University of Hong Kong. Scientific prose, terminology and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The title-page author block changes from one row of three authors to two rows of two. Main-text pagination and spacing reflow, including the conclusion moving from page 9 to page 10; the four figures and three tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The authorship/contact updates and modest layout reflow leave the scientific narrative, methods, proofs, experimental evidence and reproducibility information unchanged, including Tables 1–2 and Appendices A–K. These changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
